hints: Use the vertical displacement equation $s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ at $t = 3\text{ s}$ and $t = 4\text{ s}$.
Form the two expressions for height: $s = 3u - 45$ and $s = 4u - 80$.
Equate the two expressions to find $u = 35\text{ m s}^{-1}$, then substitute to obtain $s = 60\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
Express the vertical displacement $s$ at $t = 3\text{ s}$ and $t = 4\text{ s}$ using $s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$:
$$s = u(3) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(3^2) = 3u - 45$$
$$s = u(4) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(4^2) = 4u - 80$$

Equate the two expressions for the common height $s$:
$$4u - 80 = 3u - 45$$
$$4u - 3u = 80 - 45 \implies u = 35\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Substitute $u = 35\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the height $s$:
$$s = 3(35) - 45 = 105 - 45 = 60\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Constant-Acceleration Motion: Sets up s = 3u - 45 and s = 4u - 80, solving for u = 35 m s^-1 and s = 60 m.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the constant acceleration equation for vertical displacement under gravity ($a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$$

At time $t = 3\text{ s}$, substitute into the formula:
$$s = u(3) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(3^2) = 3u - 5(9) = 3u - 45\quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

At time $t = 4\text{ s}$, substitute into the formula:
$$s = u(4) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(4^2) = 4u - 5(16) = 4u - 80\quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Because the particle is at the same height $s$ at both times (once rising and once falling), set Equation 1 equal to Equation 2:
$$4u - 80 = 3u - 45$$

Subtract $3u$ from both sides and add 80 to both sides:
$$4u - 3u = 80 - 45$$
$$u = 35\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Substitute $u = 35\text{ m s}^{-1}$ back into Equation 1 to find $s$:
$$s = 3(35) - 45 = 105 - 45 = 60\text{ m}$$
